title: Queue convergence night probe log
content:
Context:
We ran a late-night probe to reproduce a customer-observed regression where long-tail latency spikes coincided with a drop in KV cache hit rates. The goal was to exercise the queueing/kerneldriver handshake under mixed short/long sequence load and capture metrics that were missing from the daytime incident (SRT-4212).

Quick summary of what we did:
- Time: 2026-03-15 00:30–03:10 PST (approx)
- Cluster: dev-kv-batch-staging (8xA100, 400G network)
- Workload: synthetic mix 80% short (<=64 tokens) / 20% long (>=1024 tokens), 2k qps steady for 40m with 10m bursts to 4k qps every 10m
- Runtime build: serve-runtime@sha: b7f3a2c (kernel handshake logging + adaptive-queue feature flag on)
- Clients: loadgen-v2 with header tag to force route to the same model variant used in production

Observations (high-level):
- At ~00:55, p99 generation latency jumped from baseline ~310ms to ~1.2s for ~7 minutes. During the same window, KV hit rate dropped from 92% to 63%.
- Average batch size dropped from 12->6 during the spike, but GPU occupancy remained high (~82%) — indicates many smaller batches in flight.
- Kernel transition logs show repeated micro-handshakes (~70ms each) when a long-seq request reached a worker handling many short-seq requests.
- We observed queue reordering in the re-orderer (debug logs) where some short requests were pushed behind inflight long ones due to affinity pinning; backlog then created small batches and forced more kernel handshakes.
- Memory pressure on prefill KV was low; eviction not triggered. The effect looks like synchronization/serialization rather than KV-memory capacity.

Measurements (selected):
- Baselines before spike:
  - p50: 95ms, p95: 270ms, p99: 310ms
  - mean batch size: 12.1
  - KV hit rate: 92.1%
- During spike window:
  - p50: 110ms, p95: 680ms, p99: 1.2s
  - mean batch size: 6.2
  - KV hit rate: 63.4%
  - GPU util: 82% (no thermal throttles)
  - Kernel handshake median latency: 70ms, 95th: 160ms

Logs & artifacts captured:
- Full kernel-handshake trace: s3://staging-artifacts/queue-probe/2026-03-15/handshake-trace.log
- Re-orderer debug dump: s3://staging-artifacts/queue-probe/2026-03-15/reorder-dump.json
- Loadgen config: github.com/redwood-inference/loadgen/experiments/queue-convergence-030126.yaml

Initial hypothesis (why this happened):
1) Affinity-driven reordering + long-seq arrivals create starvation for short sequences on some workers. These short sequences get delayed until they coalesce into smaller-than-optimal batches, reducing KV amortization (effective hit rate) and increasing per-request kernel handshake overhead.
2) The adaptive-queue timeout (recently tuned down to 30ms in sprint 24) tries to flush batches quickly to keep latency low. Under mixed traffic it causes more frequent batch flushes and increases handshake frequency; combined with reordering this yields the observed pattern.
3) Possible race between prefill placement logic and per-worker queue drains where KV contexts get recreated rather than reused, dropping effective hit rate.

Tested mitigations (quick experiments during the probe):
- Turned adaptive-queue timeout to 60ms (double): reduced handshake rate and raised mean batch size from 6.2 -> 10.0. p99 dropped to ~560ms but KV hit rate recovered only to ~78%.
- Disabled affinity pinning for short sequences in one worker pool: p99 improved to ~480ms, KV hit rate ~82%, but we saw more cross-worker transfers (slightly higher network tx).
- Forced KV sticky placement (keep KV context warm on first worker) for long sequences: reduced KV re-instantiation logs but had negligible effect on small-batch churn.

Action items (owners + target dates):
- Ethan: create a reproducible unit test for re-orderer that simulates pin-and-long sequence arrival pattern (due 2026-03-19).
- Samira: instrument per-worker KV context lifetime metrics and add gauge to Grafana (due 2026-03-18).
- Maya: roll out adaptive-queue timeout 45ms staged on canary group and capture impact metrics; coordinate with SRE for safe rollback (in progress, estimate 2026-03-17).
- Luca: prototype a soft-prefill flag that prevents KV context re-creation for the first 500ms after worker idle -> hot-path warm (prototype by 2026-03-22).
- All: schedule sync with re-orderer owners (eng-routing) to discuss affinity heuristics and possible backpressure signals (meeting 2026-03-17 10:00 PST).

Open questions / unresolved:
- Is the reduced KV hit rate caused mainly by smaller coalesced batches (less prefix overlap) or by KV context churn? Need finer metric breakdown.
- Does disabling affinity at scale harm throughput or just increase inter-GPU network overhead? (small-scale test looked OK).
- Can we add a backpressure signal from kernel to re-orderer to reduce pushing short requests behind long ones when handshake backlog exists?

Notes-to-self / rough ideas:
- Consider a hybrid flush rule: if a long-seq detected and there are pending short seqs, delay flush small amount (10–20ms) to allow coalescing up to SLO-friendly threshold. Might reduce p99 while keeping p50 close to baseline.
- Explore encoding request-length as a re-orderer cost metric rather than strict affinity key.
- Add a microbenchmark to measure handshake latency sensitivity to batch size for the current kernel build; use that to tune adaptive-queue default.

Quick patch pointers and links: PR 918 contains extra kernel-handshake debug logging (useful for next run); PR 927 (in draft) implements the adaptive-queue timeout toggle at route-level.

Meeting conclusion:
We reproduced the pattern and have actionable mitigations. Next run after instrumentation + small canary change (45ms adaptive timeout) scheduled for 2026-03-17 02:00 PST. Expect deeper root-cause once per-worker KV lifecycle metrics are in Grafana (Samira).

Appendix (raw scratch):
- repro steps: start loadgen with burst pattern, wait for 40m, collect handshake trace, capture reorder-dump.
- quick logs snippet:
  [00:55:07] worker-12 handshake start id=xxxx seq=long
  [00:55:07] worker-12 prefill-create ctx=kv-2385
  [00:55:07] worker-12 flush batch size=3 reason=timeout
  [00:55:07] re-orderer push short->back id=yy reason=affinity-pin

- Slack notes: pinged @eng-routing (J. Ortega) and @sre-oncall to watch canary window.

If you add anything experimental to the runtime build, please include the handshake log flag and a small sampling rate to avoid filling logs in prod.

End of probe notes.
